page: Microsoft Azure F48als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Falsv6 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark testing, the F48als_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU testing, Geekbench multi-core scores, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Single-core performance is also strong, ranking in the top 25% for Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests. The system's memory subsystem delivers top-tier performance for small-block cached reads, alongside strong large-block read and write bandwidth.

The primary tradeoff of the F48als_v6 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU and the absence of local storage. This makes it highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, such as software compilation, image processing, and medium-scale LLM inference, where it achieves top-tier text generation speeds. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference on 70B models, where its performance drops to average levels.
